items.text: A merged PR adding is-number, with an honest "Dependencies changed" section.
The evil-helper report from the unprotected install, and proof that all three controls blocked it.
A THESE PACKAGES DO NOT MATCH THE HASHES error you caused on purpose.
Dependency confusion reproduced, then fixed two ways.
The "where my bytes come from" output, and a started dependency inventory.
A verbose dependency tree with an "omitted for conflict" line, and the tree after removing the direct pin.
Your JAR and plugin counts, and the failing requirePluginVersions output.
The Downloading from vendor-plugins line that proves a mirror bypass, and the count that proves external:* caught everything else.
One refusal of each kind: not on the whitelist (Maven), DENIED (an image), and blocked by rule (APT).
"build one" then "build two: surprise" under the same SNAPSHOT version, and the strict checksum failure.
The index digest and amd64 manifest digest of node:24-bookworm-slim, the matching sha256sum, and the identical digest served by the lab registry.
One backported package explained, with its changelog line.
The identical sha256sum of the two InRelease files, then Good signature and BAD signature.
Both worksheets, and a pull request on the lab Git server with your learning log.
Both npm audit runs on audit-demo, the silent zero and the three real findings, and your gate script's three exit codes.
CycloneDX and SPDX SBOMs of your project, and an image SBOM whose subject is a digest.
Grype and Trivy totals for the same image, with the date.
A merged PR with docs/triage.md (three decisions, one dated exception, the SBOM record) and vex/node-base.openvex.json.
Scanner output showing your VEX statements as suppressed.
A merged PR removing is-number, with the SBOM diff in its description.
A merged PR with Dockerfile (pinned by digest, USER 1000:1000, HEALTHCHECK), Dockerfile.distroless, .dockerignore, .conftest/policy/, and .github/workflows/image.yml.
conftest verify passing three tests, including the placeholder-digest test you wrote after catching your own policy's bug.
The hadolint, trivy config, and Conftest results on bad.Dockerfile, and your list of problems no tool caught.
A green image run on main whose job summary shows two pushed digests, and crane digest output from the lab that matches them.
The trivy image gate result for your slim and distroless images, and the .trivyignore expiry experiment.
The fake password and token you pulled out of the leaky image's layers, and your four-step response.
dockerfile-policy listed as a required status check on protect-main.
The weak-workflow attack chain written out, and the script injection reproduced and then fixed with env:.
zizmor and actionlint output on the weak workflow and on your own (before and after pinning).
Your workflows with every uses: pinned to a SHA plus a version comment, and least-privilege permissions:.
A merged image workflow that signs the digest and writes provenance and SBOM attestations, and the run's Rekor index and attestation URL.
A cosign verify that passes for your identity and fails for a wrong one, plus a passing gh attestation verify.
The offline sign / tamper / signed-malware demo outputs.
The package firewall matrix filled in from the lab registry, including both refusal messages word for word, the lodash result with each token, and the warm-cache bypass.
The same matrix started for your company's product, with every untested row marked documented only or unknown.
docs/pipeline-threat-model.md merged through a PR that passed your hardened checks.
